description: Weak position labels for training, built by novel_ner.weak. Training chapters: 1..max_train_chapter minus the 31 dev chapters (dev_config); the test order's chapters are never labelled. Sources, in priority order: the chapter's own Opus list (name+type; same_as never makes a span), dictionary rows that apply in the chapter (scope / reveal chapter), dictionary rows blocked there, (name, type) pairs Opus listed in other training chapters. Names with a parenthesis or shorter than min_len are dropped from the dictionary; the other-chapter lexicon also keeps only names of at least min_len characters (a book-wide single character would match inside ordinary words); a chapter's own list keeps its single-character names. One left-to-right pass keeps the longest match at each position. Settings: S1 = dictionary (applying) only, positive. S2 = chapter list + dictionary (applying), positive, the chapter list's type wins. S2raw = S2 without conversions (ablation of the conversions). S3 = all four sources; listed in the chapter -> positive; otherwise uncertain (not in the loss), reason = the first source in priority order: dictionary_applies, dictionary_scope_or_reveal, other_chapters_only (later sources may back it too; uncertain rows keep their sources); a string with two types -> uncertain type_conflict. S3b = S3 plus words jieba.posseg tags nr/ns/nt/nz (>= 2 chars) in the gaps, uncertain of any type (phrase_miner). Conversions (all but S2raw): K1 a title after a person name (guide B1; title_suffixes = the B1 examples plus the same class seen in the data) is cut off when what remains is one character or a known person name, otherwise kept (S1/S2) or uncertain title_boundary (S3/S3b); K2 a person '假'+known person name -> the name (A6/B3); K3 category_words and grade+category (grade_category_pattern) -> O (E3/A2/A5); K4 a non-person name that is the tail of a longer name of the same entity (dictionary canonical, training same_as) -> kept (S1/S2) or uncertain tail_abbreviation (S3/S3b) (E4). No per-name exceptions. dictionary_cutoff = N truncates the dictionary for the learning curve (rows revealed by N whose name occurs in a training chapter <= N); null = the whole snapshot dictionary. Dev labels are built for all 31 dev chapters and scored on the answered ones only, never trained on.
